subject: Final-mile load validation and cutover window — acceptance criteria & timing
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@astra-nova.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@astra-nova.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps for capacity acceptance testing

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the call earlier. We want to lock the acceptance window for our hosted->dedicated migration. Two asks up-front: 1) can Redwood run a final throughput validation that mirrors our production burst profile (attached), and 2) we need a guaranteed swap window with rollback guardrails because we have a hard maintenance blackout the week after Thanksgiving.

Attached: an-load-profile-20261122.csv — this is a 72-hour synthetic including burst spikes up to 250 RPS for short periods.

Please confirm proposed test window and who from Redwood ops will own runbooks.

— Sanjay
VP Engineering, AstraNova
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@astra-nova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps for capacity acceptance testing

Sanjay —

Thanks for the profile and for flagging the blackout. We propose a 48-hour validation window starting Monday 2026-11-30 00:00 UTC → 2026-12-02 00:00 UTC with the swap scheduled in a 2-hour cutover slot at 2026-11-30 15:00–17:00 PST (canary + progressive ramp). Key notes:

- Redwood will run the throughput test against the dedicated pool that mirrors the CSV profile.
- Acceptance gates: 99th-pct token latency <= 450ms, sustained p50 token latency <= 120ms, no more than 1% token error increases vs hosted baseline, and model output regression score (prompt set) delta <= 2% relative to hosted baseline.
- Fallback: automated routing back to hosted runs if latency or error thresholds breach during the final 15-minute stabilization window; manual rollback allowed within 30 minutes of cutover.
- Ops owners: Karthik (capacity/gating), Ben (traffic orchestration). Michael will own the post-cutover smoke and SLA attestation.

I attached our preliminary benchmark report (rn-benchmark-report-20261125.pdf) — Karthik, Ben: please comment if the gates/timings look safe.

— Priya
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps for capacity acceptance testing

Agree with Priya's proposal, a few operational clarifications:

1) GPU sizing: based on AstraNova's profile, we will provision a mixed pool: 6x A100-80GB-equivalent (for model-peak) + 12x H100-LC-equivalent nodes to absorb bursty simultaneous sessions. Peak headroom target = 1.6x observed 95th RPS.
2) KV/prefix caching: we will seed the cache prior to cutover using traffic mirroring for 6 hours to approximate warm state — that reduces tail latency risk.
3) Continuous batching thresholds: set batching max latency 35ms and max batch size 256 for the canary; we will reduce batch size if we see token-latency drift > 10% vs baseline.
4) Pre-cutover smoke: Ben to run staged traffic (10%, 30%, 60%, 100%) across 40-minute ramps during the two-hour slot; final stabilization at 100% for 15 min.

I recommend an additional night (2026-12-01 02:00–06:00 UTC) reserved for roll-forward remediation if we encounter performance anomalies.

— Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@astra-nova.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@astra-nova.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Final-mile load validation and cutover window — acceptance criteria & timing

Sanjay/Elena —

We're lined up to run the staged ramp and mirror your production spikes. A few practical items for the runbook:

- Attachment list for ops: runbook stub (we'll upload to Drive before the run), an-load-profile-20261122.csv (you provided), rn-benchmark-report-20261125.pdf, and SLA-except-list-v2.docx (outlines exceptions for short-lived tail errors during warm-up).
- Communication plan: Slack channel #an-cutover (invite sent), Zoom standby for the 2-hour slot, and a PagerDuty escalation to Redwood SRE if latency crosses 700ms at the 99th percentile.
- Data handling: no customer payloads will be persisted; audit logs are time-limited per agreement.

Operational ask for AstraNova: sign the DocuSign cutover acknowledgement by EOD Monday 2026-11-29 so we can lock infra. Link in thread.

— Ben
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@astra-nova.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 07:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Final-mile load validation and cutover window — acceptance criteria & timing

Quick ops readiness update:

- Dedicated pool is provisioned in us-west with the exact SKU mix Karthik requested; we ran a dry cache seeding last night and observed a 12% tail improvement.
- Runbook v1 uploaded to Drive (link above) and includes step-by-step rollback commands. Will attach final runbook PDF to the DocuSign envelope before signing.
- Infra note: one H100-LC node is provisionally flagged for replacement (disk health warning). Replacement ETA 6 hours — we can still proceed because headroom remains >1.4x. Recommend we proceed but mark the node for hot-swap during the night reserve window if needed.

I'll be on call for the cutover.

— Neha
Principal Cloud Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@astra-nova.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Final-mile load validation and cutover window — acceptance criteria & timing

Team —

Thanks, all. DocuSign signed (link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/AN-4721-cutover). We reviewed the benchmark PDF and the exception doc; the AstraNova execs approved the 2-hour slot and the reserved night window for remediation. Please run the mirror seeding 6 hours prior as you noted. We'll stand up our on-call alongside Redwood ops.

Two final asks:
1) After the 15-minute stabilization at 100% please publish a one-page SLA attestation (template in Drive) and 2) include explicit rollback times in the post-cutover notes (we want timeline markers for compliance).

See you on the channel.

— Sanjay
VP Engineering, AstraNova
